bank.name: Islamic History
bank.subject: Islamic Studies
bank.description: Major Islamic dynasties, conquests and figures: from the Rashidun era to the Ottomans and Muslim South Asia.

questions.prompt: Islam entered the Indian subcontinent through which conquest in 711 CE?
options: Muhammad bin Qasim's conquest of Sindh
questions.explanation: Muhammad bin Qasim conquered Sindh in 711 CE, opening the subcontinent to Islam.

questions.prompt: Muhammad bin Qasim defeated which ruler of Sindh?
questions.explanation: Raja Dahir was the Hindu ruler of Sindh defeated by Muhammad bin Qasim.

questions.prompt: The Umayyad dynasty had its capital in which city?
questions.explanation: The Umayyads ruled from Damascus (661-750 CE).

questions.prompt: Who founded the Umayyad dynasty?
questions.explanation: Muawiyah ibn Abi Sufyan (RA) founded the Umayyad dynasty in 661 CE.

questions.prompt: The Abbasid dynasty ruled from which capital?
questions.explanation: The Abbasids ruled from Baghdad (750-1258 CE).

questions.prompt: The Abbasid Caliphate came to an end in which year, after the Mongol sack of Baghdad?
questions.explanation: Hulagu Khan's Mongols sacked Baghdad in 1258, ending the Abbasids.

questions.prompt: The famous 'House of Wisdom' (Bayt al-Hikmah) was established in?
questions.explanation: The House of Wisdom, a great library and translation centre, flourished in Baghdad.

questions.prompt: Which Abbasid caliph is associated with the Islamic Golden Age and the Arabian Nights?
questions.explanation: Harun al-Rashid (786-809) ruled during the peak of the Golden Age.

questions.prompt: The Ottoman Empire was founded by?
questions.explanation: Osman I (d. 1326) founded the Ottoman dynasty.

questions.prompt: Constantinople was conquered by the Ottomans under which Sultan in 1453?
questions.explanation: Mehmed II, the Conqueror, took Constantinople in 1453.

questions.prompt: The Ottoman Caliphate was formally abolished in which year?
questions.explanation: Mustafa Kemal Ataturk abolished the caliphate in 1924.

questions.prompt: Which Ottoman sultan is known as 'the Lawgiver' and 'the Magnificent'?
questions.explanation: Suleiman the Magnificent (1520-1566) is called Kanuni, the Lawgiver.

questions.prompt: Sultan Salahuddin Ayyubi recaptured Jerusalem from the Crusaders in which year?
questions.explanation: Salahuddin (Saladin) liberated Jerusalem in 1187 after the Battle of Hattin.

questions.prompt: The Battle of Hattin (1187), which opened the way to Jerusalem, was fought between?
questions.explanation: Saladin's forces defeated the Crusader army at Hattin.

questions.prompt: Muslim rule in Spain (Andalus) came to an end in which year?
questions.explanation: Granada fell to the Spanish in 1492, ending 781 years of Muslim presence.

questions.prompt: Who led the Muslim conquest of Spain in 711 CE?
questions.explanation: Tariq ibn Ziyad led the crossing into Spain; Gibraltar is named after him (Jabal Tariq).

questions.prompt: The Mughal Empire in India was founded by Babur after the Battle of Panipat in?
questions.explanation: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi at the First Battle of Panipat in 1526.

questions.prompt: Which Mughal emperor is known for his policy of religious tolerance and Sulh-i-Kul?
questions.explanation: Akbar (1556-1605) promoted universal tolerance.

questions.prompt: The first ruler of the Delhi Sultanate was?
questions.explanation: Qutb-ud-din Aibak founded the Delhi Sultanate (Mamluk dynasty) in 1206.

questions.prompt: Shah Waliullah, the great 18th-century revivalist scholar, lived in?
questions.explanation: Shah Waliullah Dehlawi (1703-1762) lived and taught in Delhi.

questions.prompt: Egypt was conquered by the Muslims during the caliphate of?
questions.explanation: Amr ibn al-As conquered Egypt in 640 CE under Umar (RA).

questions.prompt: The dynasty founded by Salahuddin Ayyubi is known as?
questions.explanation: Salahuddin founded the Ayyubid dynasty of Egypt and Syria.

questions.prompt: The Great Mosque of Cordoba was begun by?
questions.explanation: Abd al-Rahman I, the Umayyad prince of Spain, began the mosque in 785 CE.

questions.prompt: Which Abbasid caliph is famous for patronising the translation of Greek works into Arabic?
questions.explanation: Al-Ma'mun (813-833) strongly supported the translation movement.

questions.prompt: The Battle of Tours (Poitiers) in 732 CE, which halted the Muslim advance in Europe, was fought against?
questions.explanation: Charles Martel's Franks stopped the Umayyad advance at Tours in 732.

questions.prompt: The city of Baghdad was founded by which Abbasid caliph?
questions.explanation: Al-Mansur founded Baghdad in 762 CE as the new Abbasid capital.

questions.prompt: The Seljuk commander Alp Arslan defeated the Byzantines at Manzikert in?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Manzikert (1071) opened Anatolia to the Turks.

questions.prompt: Which Muslim ruler of Ghazni led seventeen campaigns into India?
questions.explanation: Sultan Mahmud of Ghazni (998-1030) carried out seventeen raids into India.

questions.prompt: Who was the founder of the Abbasid dynasty?
questions.explanation: Abu al-Abbas as-Saffah founded the Abbasid dynasty in 750 CE.

questions.prompt: Baghdad was sacked by which Mongol leader in 1258, ending the Abbasid caliphate?
questions.explanation: Hulagu Khan sacked Baghdad in 1258, destroying the Abbasid caliphate.

questions.prompt: The Fatimid dynasty ruled from which city?
questions.explanation: The Fatimids (909-1171) ruled from Cairo, which they founded in 969 CE.

questions.prompt: Who recaptured Jerusalem from the Crusaders in 1187?
questions.explanation: Salahuddin Ayyubi (Saladin) liberated Jerusalem in 1187 at the Battle of Hattin.

questions.prompt: Salahuddin belonged to which dynasty?
questions.explanation: Salahuddin founded the Ayyubid dynasty (1171-1260).

questions.prompt: Which Mamluk sultan defeated the Mongols at the Battle of Ain Jalut in 1260?
questions.explanation: Qutuz led the Mamluks to victory at Ain Jalut, halting the Mongol advance into the Muslim world.

questions.prompt: The Ottoman Empire reached its peak under which sultan?
questions.explanation: Suleiman the Magnificent (1520-1566) ruled at the empire's zenith.

questions.prompt: Muslim rule in Spain (Al-Andalus) began in which year?
questions.explanation: Tariq ibn Ziyad crossed into Spain in 711 CE, beginning Muslim rule of Al-Andalus.

questions.prompt: The last Muslim stronghold in Spain, Granada, fell in which year?
questions.explanation: Granada fell to Ferdinand and Isabella in 1492, ending Muslim rule in Spain.

questions.prompt: Which dynasty built the famous Alhambra palace in Granada?
questions.explanation: The Nasrids built the Alhambra in the 13th-14th centuries.

questions.prompt: Which ruler of Al-Andalus proclaimed himself caliph, rivaling Baghdad?
questions.explanation: Abd al-Rahman III declared the Caliphate of Cordoba in 929 CE.

questions.prompt: The Seljuk Turks defeated the Byzantines at which battle in 1071, opening Anatolia?
questions.explanation: Alp Arslan's victory at Manzikert (1071) opened Anatolia to Turkish settlement.

questions.prompt: Who defeated the Byzantines at the Battle of Manzikert?
questions.explanation: Seljuk sultan Alp Arslan won at Manzikert in 1071.

questions.prompt: The First Crusade captured Jerusalem in which year?
questions.explanation: The First Crusade took Jerusalem in 1099, establishing Crusader states.

questions.prompt: Which caliphate is known as the 'Golden Age of Islam' for science and learning?
questions.explanation: The Abbasid era (8th-13th centuries) saw the translation movement and great scientific advances.

questions.prompt: Which European language borrowed many scientific terms from Arabic during the Golden Age?
questions.explanation: Words like algebra, algorithm, alchemy and zero entered Latin and Spanish from Arabic.

questions.prompt: The Silk Road connected the Muslim world with which region?
questions.explanation: The Silk Road linked China, Central Asia and the Middle East, enriching trade and knowledge.

questions.prompt: The Umayyad caliphate was overthrown by whom in 750 CE?
questions.explanation: The Abbasid Revolution replaced the Umayyads in 750 CE.

questions.prompt: Who was the fifth Umayyad caliph, famous for reforms and the gold dinar?
questions.explanation: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz (r. 717-720) is famed for justice and reforms; Abd al-Malik introduced the dinar.

questions.prompt: Which Umayyad caliph built the Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: Abd al-Malik (r. 685-705) built the Dome of the Rock, completed in 691 CE.

questions.prompt: The Al-Aqsa Mosque was built during which caliph's reign?
questions.explanation: Al-Aqsa was constructed under Umayyad caliph Al-Walid I (r. 705-715).

questions.prompt: Which Muslim leader fought against the Third Crusade alongside Saladin?
options: Richard the Lionheart was his opponent; no Muslim ally is famed
questions.explanation: Saladin faced Richard I in the Third Crusade; the two made the Treaty of Jaffa in 1192.

questions.prompt: Which event in 1916 saw Arabs revolt against the Ottomans with British support?
questions.explanation: The Arab Revolt of 1916, led by Sharif Hussein, opposed Ottoman rule during World War I.

questions.prompt: The Battle of Yarmouk resulted in the Muslim conquest of:
questions.explanation: Yarmouk (636 CE) opened Syria to Muslim rule.

questions.prompt: The Battle of Qadisiyyah led to the conquest of:
questions.explanation: Qadisiyyah (637 CE) ended Sassanid rule in Iraq.

questions.prompt: Which caliph established the first Islamic navy?
questions.explanation: Under Uthman's reign the Islamic navy was developed.

questions.prompt: The Abbasid caliphate was established in which year?
questions.explanation: The Abbasids took power in 750 CE.

questions.prompt: The capital of the Abbasid caliphate was:
questions.explanation: Baghdad was founded as the Abbasid capital in 762 CE.

questions.prompt: The Dome of the Rock was built by:
questions.explanation: Abdul Malik built the Dome of the Rock in 691 CE.

questions.prompt: The Umayyad Caliphate of Spain (Al-Andalus) was founded by:
questions.explanation: Abdur Rahman I established the Spanish Umayyad state.

questions.prompt: The Muslim general who conquered Spain was:
questions.explanation: Tariq bin Ziyad led the conquest of Iberia in 711 CE.

questions.prompt: Who is known as the 'Umar II of the Umayyads'?
questions.explanation: Umar bin Abdul Aziz was famous for justice and piety.

questions.prompt: The 'Battle of Tours' (732 CE) halted Muslim advance into:
questions.explanation: Tours stopped the Muslim advance into France.

questions.prompt: The Fatimid caliphate was based in:
questions.explanation: The Fatimids ruled from Cairo.

questions.prompt: Saladin (Salahuddin Ayyubi) recaptured Jerusalem from the Crusaders in:
questions.explanation: Saladin retook Jerusalem in 1187.

questions.prompt: The Mongol sack of Baghdad occurred in:
questions.explanation: Hulagu Khan sacked Baghdad in 1258, ending the Abbasid caliphate.

questions.prompt: Constantinople was conquered by the Ottomans in:
questions.explanation: Mehmed II conquered Constantinople in 1453.

questions.prompt: Which Ottoman sultan was called 'the Lawgiver' (Kanuni)?
questions.explanation: Suleiman codified laws and expanded the empire.

questions.prompt: The Mamluk Sultanate was based in:
questions.explanation: The Mamluks ruled Egypt and Syria.

questions.prompt: The Ottoman caliphate was abolished in:
questions.explanation: Ataturk abolished the caliphate in 1924.

questions.prompt: The Fatimid dynasty was founded by whom?
questions.explanation: Ubayd Allah al-Mahdi founded the Fatimid dynasty in 909 CE.

questions.prompt: The Fatimids claimed descent from whom?
questions.explanation: The Fatimids traced their lineage to Fatimah (RA) and Ali (RA).

questions.prompt: The Ayyubid dynasty was replaced by whom?
questions.explanation: The Mamluks took over Egypt after the Ayyubids in the mid-13th century.

questions.prompt: Who is regarded as the founder of the Mamluk Sultanate of Egypt?
questions.explanation: Aybak founded the Mamluk Sultanate after the Ayyubid collapse.

questions.prompt: The Umayyad capital in Spain was?
questions.explanation: Cordoba was the capital of Muslim Spain.

questions.prompt: Who was the last Muslim ruler of Granada, who surrendered in 1492?
questions.explanation: Muhammad XII, called Boabdil, handed Granada to Ferdinand and Isabella.

questions.prompt: After the fall of Granada in 1492, the Muslims and Jews of Spain were?
questions.explanation: The Reconquista was followed by forced conversions, the Inquisition and expulsions.

questions.prompt: Mehmed II, the conqueror of Constantinople, is also known as?
questions.explanation: Mehmed II is called Fatih, the Conqueror.

questions.prompt: The Ottoman victory at Kosovo took place in which year?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Kosovo in 1389 opened the Balkans to the Ottomans.

questions.prompt: The fall of Constantinople in 1453 ended which empire?
options: The Roman Empire of the West
questions.explanation: Constantinople's fall ended the Byzantine Empire.

questions.prompt: The Ottomans rose from the ruins of which Anatolian state?
questions.explanation: The Ottoman beylik grew out of the Seljuk Sultanate of Rum.

questions.prompt: Which dynasty made Twelver Shi'ism the state religion of Persia?
questions.explanation: Shah Ismail I founded the Safavid dynasty and established Shi'ism in Iran.

questions.prompt: The Ottoman Empire's main eastern rival was?
questions.explanation: The Safavids of Persia were the Ottomans' great eastern rival.

questions.prompt: The Chishti Sufi order in the Indian subcontinent was founded by?
questions.explanation: Khwaja Muin-ud-din Chishti founded the Chishti order at Ajmer.

questions.prompt: The Sufi saint Ali Hajveri of Lahore is popularly known as?
questions.explanation: Ali Hajveri, buried in Lahore, is called Data Ganj Bakhsh.

questions.prompt: The Naqshbandi Sufi order is named after whom?
questions.explanation: The Naqshbandi order takes its name from Baha-ud-din Naqshband.

questions.prompt: The 18th-century revivalist movement in Arabia was founded by?
questions.explanation: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab launched the reform movement in Najd.

questions.prompt: Which institution did Sir Syed Ahmad Khan found in 1875?
options: The MAO College (later Aligarh Muslim University)
questions.explanation: Sir Syed founded the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College at Aligarh.

questions.prompt: Darul Uloom Deoband was founded in 1866 by whom?
questions.explanation: Nanautawi and Rashid Ahmad Gangohi established Darul Uloom Deoband.

questions.prompt: Prominent leaders of the Khilafat Movement included?
options: Maulana Muhammad Ali and Shaukat Ali
Abul Kalam Azad and Maulana Maududi
questions.explanation: The Ali brothers led the Khilafat movement in India.

questions.prompt: The Ottoman Empire entered World War I in which year?
questions.explanation: The Ottomans joined the Central Powers in 1914.

questions.prompt: The Treaty of Sevres (1920) imposed terms on which empire?
questions.explanation: Sevres partitioned the Ottoman lands after WWI.

questions.prompt: The Ottoman Caliphate was abolished in 1924 by whom?
questions.explanation: Atatürk's republic abolished the caliphate in March 1924.

questions.prompt: In 1517, the Ottomans defeated the Mamluks at which battle?
questions.explanation: The victory at Ridaniya brought Egypt and Syria under Ottoman rule.

questions.prompt: After the sack of Baghdad, a 'shadow' Abbasid caliphate continued in which city?
questions.explanation: The Mamluks hosted a puppet Abbasid caliphate in Cairo until 1517.

questions.prompt: Before the Ottomans, the holy cities of Makkah and Madinah were under whom?
questions.explanation: The Mamluks of Egypt protected the Hijaz before 1517.

questions.prompt: The Ottoman sultan Selim I conquered which regions in 1517?
questions.explanation: Selim I added Egypt, Syria and the Hijaz to the empire.

questions.prompt: The Ottoman admiral Khair ad-Din is known in Europe as?
questions.explanation: Khair ad-Din Pasha, the great Ottoman admiral, was called Barbarossa.

questions.prompt: The Khwarezmshah empire was destroyed by whom?
questions.explanation: Genghis Khan's campaigns in 1219-1221 wiped out the Khwarezmshahs.

questions.prompt: The Mongol invasions under Genghis Khan devastated which regions?
questions.explanation: Genghis Khan's armies ravaged Central Asia, Iran and Afghanistan.

questions.prompt: The Timurid dynasty was founded by whom?
questions.explanation: Timur founded the Timurid dynasty in the 14th century.

questions.prompt: The Ayyubid capital was?
questions.explanation: The Ayyubids ruled from Cairo.
